ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows triangle ABC drawn on a square grid. Points B and C lie on the same horizontal grid line, forming a horizontal base BC. Point A is above that base. The vertical grid line through A meets the line BC at a grid point D that is 1 grid unit to the left of C. Counting grid squares in the image, A is 3 grid units above BC. Reasoning: Drop the perpendicular AD to BC. Since the grid is square, AD is vertical and BC is horizontal, so AD ⟂ BC. From the grid, AD = 3 and DC = 1. In right triangle ACD, AC = sqrt(AD^2 + DC^2) = sqrt(3^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(10). Angle ACB is the same as angle ACD because D lies on BC. Therefore, cos(angle ACB) = adjacent/hypotenuse = DC/AC = 1/sqrt(10) = sqrt(10)/10.

method.method_draft: First read the grid diagram by assigning coordinates from the visible grid. Take C as the origin, let the positive x-direction point right and positive y-direction point up. From the image, B is 4 grid units left of C, so vector CB=(-4,0), and A is 1 grid unit left and 3 grid units above C, so vector CA=(-1,3). From the text, the desired angle is angle ACB, the angle between rays CA and CB. Use the vector dot-product formula: cos(angle ACB)=(CA dot CB)/(|CA||CB|). Compute CA dot CB=(-1)(-4)+3(0)=4, |CA|=sqrt(10), and |CB|=4, giving cos(angle ACB)=4/(4sqrt(10))=1/sqrt(10)=sqrt(10)/10.
